texts.preamble: Uma Shankar Maurya vs State Of U.P. on 8 December, 2023 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:233419 Court No. - 69 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 894 of 2010 Revisionist :- Uma Shankar Maurya
texts.facts: It is further prayed that the revisionist may be released on bail during the pendency of the revision before this Hon'ble Court. It is also prayed that the realisation of the fine against the revisionist may be stayed during the pendency of the revision before this Hon'ble Court." 4. The present revision was admitted vide order dated 09.03.2010 and the revisionist was directed to be released on bail. 5. The facts of the case are that on 29.12.1991 at about 02:30 p.m. Food Inspector Raj Narayan Singh went to the shop of the revisionist for inspection wherein on suspicion he purchased 450 gm carom seed from the revisionist. The said material was sent for analysis to the Food Analyst on 29.12.1991. Food analyst vide his report dated 29.02.1992 opined that the material was found to be having 2-3 % excess from the prescribed limit which was injurious to the public health. The sample was thus found to be adulterated. Sanction from the C.M.O. concerned was sought after which the complaint was filed. The trial court vide order dated 05.10.1993 framed the charges against the accused/revisionist for offences under Sections 7(i) read with Section 2(ia)(a)(l) and Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The trial in the matter started in which Raj Narayan was examined as P.W.-1 and Ashok Kumar Srivastava food clerk was examined as P.W.-2. The accused denied the prosecution case in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. Bhola was examined as D.W.-1 and Uma Shankar was examined as DW-2 from the side of the revisionist in defense. The present revision has thus been filed before this Court against both the impugned judgements and orders.
texts.arguments: 6. Learned counsel for the revisionist has argued that the notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been sent to the revisionist. It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that the same has been sent by the Food Inspector or received by the revisionist and as such valuable right of the accused/revisionist safeguarding his interest is violated. To buttress the arguments learned counsel has placed the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs. State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763 (para-14 and 15) and Narayan Prasad Sahu vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87 (para-5, 6, 8 and 9). While further elaborating the arguments it is argued that as per Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, report of food analyst has to be sent within a period of 10 days from the date of receipt of the same, but in the Uma Shankar Maurya vs State Of U.P. on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173823138/ 2 present case the said report has not been sent which clearly frustrates the purpose and valuable rights of a person to get the sample of the same retested by the Central Food Laboratory. It is argued that the Apex Court has, in no uncertain terms, in the judgement of Vijendra case (supra) has held that failure of the trial court to take into consideration that no evidence was brought on record to indicate that the report which has been claimed to be dispatched, was actually sent or delivered for the purpose of further reference to the Central Food Laboratory, if the accused is dis-satisfied with the said report. It is further argued that even the trial has failed to take note of the said fact and also to record a finding that there is no evidence to show that the said report has been received at the end of the accused/revisionist. The said safeguard is provided to the accused under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. It is argued that the present revision thus deserved to be allowed on the said two counts. 7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer and the present revision. It is argued that in the shop of the revisionist carom seed purchased by the Food Inspector which was found to be having 2-3% excess from the prescribed limit. It is argued that since the report, as per Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, was sent to the revisionist by a registered post, there was a presumption of it being delivered, more so there is nothing on record to show that the same was not delivered to him. He submits that the material was found to be adulterated and as such looking to the said fact, the present revision be dismissed.
